source: Shem Tov Hebrew Matthew (Even Bochan, Ibn Shaprut c. 1385; critical text ed. G. Howard, base ms British Library Add. 26964)

verses.translation: Then{H227} Yeshua{H3442} spoke{H1696} to the people{H5971} and to his disciples{H8527},

textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק צ״ו (Perek 96) begins here.

verses.translation: saying{H559}: On the seat{H3678} of Moshe{H4872} sit{H3427} the Perushim{H6567} and the sages{H2450}.

one_way_hebrew: כסא משה — 'the seat of Moses': the rabbinic institution by its rabbinic name (the qatedra de-Moshe of the synagogue; cf. Pesiqta deRav Kahana 1:7); a Hebrew text names the furniture of its own world.

verses.translation: And now{H6258}, all{H3605} that HE says{H559} to you, keep{H8104} and do{H6213}; but according to their ordinances{H8626} and their deeds{H4639} do not do{H6213}, for they{H1992} say{H559} and do not do{H6213}.

one_way_hebrew: תקנות (from תקן, H8626 — Ecclesiastes' verb, Eccl 1:15; 7:13; 12:9) — 'their ORDINANCES': the rabbis' own technical term for rabbinic enactments (taqqanot). The Hebrew sentence distinguishes exactly what the halakhic world distinguishes — Moses' word versus their taqqanot and precedents; Greek 'their works' (τὰ ἔργα αὐτῶν) cannot name the category.
greek_deviations: THE VERB IS SINGULAR: 'all that HE says to you' (יאמר) — he who sits on Moses' seat speaking Moses' words, i.e. keep what MOSES says. Greek Matthew reads 'all whatsoever THEY bid you, observe and do' — creating the famous contradiction with the next clause. The Hebrew has no contradiction: do what he (Moses) says; do not do their ordinances. All other mss (ABDEFG) read the plural יאמרו with the Greek; the base ms alone preserves the singular — the harder and the coherent reading.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (23:3): יאמר] יאמרו ABDEFG; ועתה] מעתה EF; שמרו ועשו] תעשו ותשמרו G; ובתקנותיהם] וכתקנותיהם ABDEG, וכתקנותיכם F (the transcriber's footnote also prefers כ: 'according to their taqqanot'); ומעשיהם] וכמעשיהם E, וכמעשיכם F; והם] omit ABDEFG.

verses.translation: And they demand{H1875} and lay{H5414} great{H1419} burdens{H4853} that men cannot{H3201} bear{H5445}, but they themselves are not willing{H7521} even to move{H5128} them with their finger{H676}.

one_way_hebrew: משאות... לסובלם — burden (משא, H4853) and the bearing-verb סבל (H5445): Isaiah's pair for idols loaded on weary beasts (Isa 46:1-2) against the God who himself carries (ואני אסבל, Isa 46:4). The teachers load; they do not carry.
דורשים — the same root as the expositor's darash (cf. 21:17; 23:14): their demanding and their preaching are one word.
translation_notes: אפי׳ — the ms abbreviates אפילו ('even'), rabbinic Hebrew's own particle.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (23:4): the whole verse omitted in C; לסובלם] + שכמי בני האדם A (שכמי אדם BDG, שכמי האדם EF) — 'on the shoulders of men,' matching the Greek; אפי׳] אפילו BG.

verses.translation: And all{H3605} their deeds{H4639} they do{H6213} for the sight{H4758} of eyes{H5869}; and they wear{H3847} costly{H3368} garments{H4403}, and large{H1419} tsitsiyot{H6734} — called fiblios —

one_way_hebrew: ציציות (H6734) — the tzitzit of Num 15:38-39 by their Torah name, enlarged for show — the very verses that command the fringe 'that ye seek not after your own heart and your own eyes' are flaunted 'for the sight of eyes.' The Hebrew's irony runs on Num 15's own words.
למראה עינים — 'for the sight of the eyes': 1 Sam 16:7's contrast (האדם יראה לעינים, 'man looks on the eyes' appearance') and Isa 11:3 (ולא למראה עיניו ישפוט).
greek_deviations: No phylacteries: Greek Matthew has 'they make broad their φυλακτήρια' — the Hebrew text has only the costly garments and the large tsitsiyot, glossed with the foreign word פיב״ליאוס (fiblios) for readers who knew church vocabulary — the same one-way glossing as evangeli (24:14) and Antichristos (24:15): the Hebrew word is native, the foreign word is the visitor.
translation_notes: פיב״ליאוס — printed pointed (פִיבְ״לִיאוֹס); points stripped here. The transcriber's footnote can only guess at the word ('fiblio~?'); Howard renders 'called phiblios.'
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (23:5): וכל...עושים] omit C; the loanword is spelled variously — פיבלאש A, פיבליואש BF, פיביליאוש D, differently again EG.

verses.translation: They love{H157} to recline first{H7223} in the banquet{H4960} houses{H1004}, and to have their seat{H4186} in the houses of assembly in the first place{H7223},

one_way_hebrew: בתי כנסיות — the synagogues by their own Hebrew name (batei kenesiyot); Greek συναγωγή is the translation of this. מסובים — 'reclining,' the rabbinic term for banqueting (the Seder's word); בתי משתאות — Esther's banquet-house vocabulary (משתה, Esth 1:3).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (23:6): בבתי כנסיות בראשונה] reordered ABDEFG; בראשונה] ראשונה A, ראשון BDEFG; להיות²] להיותם A.

verses.translation: and to be bowed down to{H7812} in the streets{H2351}, and to be called{H7121} rabbanim,

one_way_hebrew: רבנים — the title itself, in its Hebrew plural: Greek ῥαββί can only transliterate the word this text natively declines.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (23:7): ולקוראם] ולקראם EF, ולקראת להם G.

verses.translation: but you{H859}, do not desire{H7521} to be called{H7121} rabbanim: one{H259} is your rav, and all{H3605} of you are brothers{H251}.

one_way_hebrew: אחד הוא רבכם — 'ONE is your rav': the sentence leans on the Shema's אחד (Deut 6:4); the argument from the One against the titles only sounds in Hebrew.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (23:8): רבכם...אחים] omit D (haplography).

verses.translation: And call{H7121} no man{H120} on the earth{H776} father{H1}: one{H259} is your Father{H1} who is in heaven{H8064}.

one_way_hebrew: אביכם שבשמים — 'your Father who is in heaven': the fixed Hebrew liturgical phrase (avinu she-ba-shamayim), with the rabbinic ש-relative; the Greek ὁ πατὴρ ὁ οὐράνιος translates a formula this text writes natively.
textual_notes: The circulating transcription reads על תקראו; Howard's text reads אל תקראו, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (23:9): ואב...הוא] omit D (haplography — see on 23:8).

verses.translation: And do not be called{H7121} rabbanim, for your rav is one{H259} — the Mashiach{H4899}.

textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (23:10): שרבכם] שרביכם C; אחד] omit EF.

verses.translation: The greatest{H1419} among{H996} you will be your minister{H8334}.

one_way_hebrew: משרת (H8334) — again the sanctuary-service word (as at 20:26-28): greatness defined by the priest's verb of ministering.

verses.translation: And he who exalts himself{H7311} will be brought low{H7817}, and he who is brought low{H7817} will be exalted{H7311}.

one_way_hebrew: רום/שח — the exact word-pair of Isaiah's day-of-YHWH oracle: 'the loftiness (רום) of man shall be bowed down (ושח)' (Isa 2:11,17; cf. 2:9). The saying is Isa 2 compressed to its two verbs; Greek ὑψωθήσεται/ταπεινωθήσεται translates the sense and loses the source.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (23:12): ירום] יתרומם A; ישח²] omit EF.

verses.translation: Woe{H188} to you, Perushim{H6567} and sages{H2450}, hypocrites{H2611} — the kingdom{H4438} of heaven{H8064} before{H6440} the sons{H1121} of man{H120} — and those who wish{H7521} to come in{H935} you do not allow{H5800} to come in.

one_way_hebrew: חנפים (H2611) — Job's word for the godless dissembler (Job 8:13; 13:16), the Hebrew behind every 'hypocrite' in this chapter; Greek ὑποκριτής ('stage-actor') is the theater's metaphor, חנף the covenant's.
translation_notes: The base ms lost two phrases by haplography; the sense (with BDEFG and ABDEFG) is: '...hypocrites, (for you shut) the kingdom of heaven before the sons of men; (you yourselves do not enter,) and those who wish to enter you do not allow to enter.' Howard's English prints the supplied phrases in parentheses.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק צ״ז (Perek 97) begins here.
The circulating transcription reads והכחמים and וארוצים; Howard's text reads והחכמים and והרוצים, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (23:13): חנפים] + שאתם סוגרים BDEFG ('for you shut'); אדם] + אתם אינכם באים ABDEFG ('you yourselves do not come in'); אדם] האדם DEF; והרוצים] והרוצה A.

verses.translation: Woe{H188} to you, Perushim{H6567} and sages{H2450}, hypocrites{H2611}, for you devour{H398} and divide{H2505} the wealth{H5233} of the widowed{H490} women{H802} with long{H752} exposition{H1875}; and on account{H5668} of this you will bear{H5445} a long punishment.

one_way_hebrew: בדרש ארוך — 'with a long DERASH': the Hebrew names the instrument — the homiletic exposition of the study-house (the darash of midrash) — where Greek has 'for a pretence making long prayer.' The satire is in-house: the sermon eats the widow's house.
אלמנות (H490) — the widow, whose case is the Torah's own test of justice (Exod 22:21; Deut 27:19; Isa 10:2, 'that widows may be their spoil').
greek_deviations: This 'widows' woe stands in Shem Tov (as in the Byzantine text and KJV of 23:14) in the order 13-then-14; the oldest Greek mss lack the verse entirely. In the Hebrew it is native text with no recorded variant against its presence.

'You will bear a LONG punishment' (עונש ארך) — Greek has 'the greater damnation' (περισσότερον κρίμα); the Hebrew answers the long sermon with a long sentence — measure for measure, in matching adjectives (ארוך/ארך).
textual_notes: The circulating transcription reads הנשים ואלמנות; Howard's text reads הנשים האלמנות, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (23:14): הנשים] omit G; זה] omit EF; ארוך] ארך ABC, omit EF.

verses.translation: You circle{H5437} the sea{H3220} and the dry land{H3004} to bind{H7194} the heart{H3820} of one{H259} man{H376} to your faith{H530}; and when he is bound{H7194}, he becomes evil{H7451} double{H3718} what he was before{H6924}.

one_way_hebrew: הים והיבשה — sea and dry land by their creation names (Gen 1:9-10; Jonah 1:9, 'YHWH... which hath made the sea and the dry land'): the missionaries traverse the Maker's whole map to capture one heart.

לקשור לב — 'to BIND the heart': the Hebrew names proselytizing as binding (קשר, H7194), and the convert as נקשר, 'bound' — a tied soul, not a won one. Greek 'to make one proselyte' loses the cord-figure the verse turns on.
greek_deviations: 'He becomes twice as evil as BEFORE' — Greek Matthew reads 'twofold more the child of hell (υἱὸν γεέννης) than yourselves.' The Hebrew measures the convert against his own past, not against Gehinnom and not against his teachers.
textual_notes: The circulating transcription reads בקשר; Howard's text reads נקשר, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (23:15): רע] רעב EF; וכאשר] כאשר EF; לב] omit G.

verses.translation: Woe{H188} to you, council{H4186} of the blind{H5787}, who say{H559} that he who swears{H7650} by the Sanctuary{H1964} is not liable{H2325}, but he who vows{H5087} by any thing{H1697} that is dedicated{H6942} to the building{H1146} of the Sanctuary{H1964} is liable{H2325} to pay{H7999}.

one_way_hebrew: חייב / אינו חייב — 'liable / not liable': the Mishnah's own verdict-pair, the standing formula of tractate Shevuot on oaths. The woe argues inside halakhic categories — swearing (נשבע) versus vowing (ידור, Num 30:3's distinction) and dedicated property (נקדש, the heqdesh of the Temple treasury) — vocabulary no Greek writer owns.
מושבי — 'the seat/session' (מושב) of the blind: the word of Ps 1:1 (מושב לצים, 'the seat of the scorners') and Ps 107:32 (מושב זקנים, 'the session of elders'); Howard renders 'council of the blind.'
greek_deviations: No GOLD: Greek Matthew contrasts the temple with 'the gold of the temple'; the Hebrew contrasts the Sanctuary with 'whatever is DEDICATED to the building of the Sanctuary' — the halakhic institution of heqdesh, not the glitter. (Greek 23:16 does have its counterpart here, as Howard's text and English both show — it is v. 21, not v. 16, that is missing from this family; see on v. 20.)
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (23:16): אשר תאמרו] שתאמרו H; נקדש] נקשר A; לבניין ההיכל] להיכל ולבנינו H.

verses.translation: Madmen{H7696} and blind{H5787}! Which{H335} is greater{H1419} — the Sanctuary{H1964}, or the thing{H1697} dedicated{H6942} to the Sanctuary{H1964}?

one_way_hebrew: משוגעים (H7696) — Deut 28:34's madness (משגע ממראה עיניך); Greek μωροί ('fools') is tamer than the Hebrew's charge of derangement.
textual_notes: The circulating transcription omits דבר; Howard's text reads או דבר הנקדש להיכל, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (23:17): דבר] הדבר ABGH; איזה] איזהו ADEFGH; להיכל] לו G.

verses.translation: And he who swears{H7650} by the altar{H4196} is not liable{H2325}, but he who swears{H7650} that he will offer{H7126} an offering{H7133} is liable{H2325} to give{H5414} it.

one_way_hebrew: קרבן (H7133) — the korban of Leviticus (Lev 1:2), the Temple's own word for an offering; Greek δῶρον ('gift') generalizes it. Mark 7:11 must transliterate this very word (κορβᾶν) and explain it to Greek readers — here it needs no gloss.
textual_notes: The circulating transcription omits קרבן and reads הייב; Howard's text reads שיקריב קרבן חייב, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (23:18): ישבע] נשבע D.

verses.translation: Which{H335} is more{H3148} — the offering{H7133}, or the altar{H4196} that sanctifies{H6942} the offering{H7133}?

translation_notes: The printed text repeats או before the second הקרבן ('the offering or the altar, the sanctifier or the offering?' — so Howard's English: 'which is more, the gift or the altar, the temple or the gift?'); the sense, as in the Greek ('the altar that sanctifieth the gift'), takes המקדש as the participle governing הקרבן, and the translation follows it.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (23:19): mss ABDEFG open the verse with אוי העורים ('Woe, blind ones' — cf. Greek 'ye fools and blind'); איזה] איזהו ACDEFG.

verses.translation: He who swears{H7650} by the altar{H4196} swears{H7650} by it and by all{H3605} that is within{H8432} it.

translation_notes: The base text reads נשבע without בו ('swears — and by all that is in it'); ms A adds בו ('by it'), which Howard's English supplies in parentheses and the translation follows.
textual_notes: The circulating transcription reads ישבו; Howard's text reads ישבע, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (23:20): נשבע] + בו A; G rewords the close (אשר בתוכו).

Greek 23:21 ('and whoso shall swear by the sanctuary, sweareth by it, and by him that dwelleth therein') has no counterpart in the Shem Tov text: Howard's apparatus states 'Vs 21 omitted by all mss,' and his Hebrew and English both run directly from v. 20 to v. 22.

verses.translation: And he who swears{H7650} by the throne{H3678} of Elohim{H430} swears{H7650} by it and by him who sits{H3427} upon it.

one_way_hebrew: כסא... וביושב עליו — the throne and 'him who SITS upon it': Isa 6:1's enthroned One (ישב על כסא) and Ps 47:9. The oath-chain ends where Isaiah's vision begins.
greek_deviations: Greek Matthew reads 'he that shall swear by HEAVEN, sweareth by the throne of God'; the Hebrew goes straight to the throne — heaven never enters the chain, because v. 21's sanctuary-link is also absent from this family.
textual_notes: First occurrence in this chapter of אלקים — the ms uses the reverent ק-spelling.
Howard's apparatus (23:22): ישבע] נשבע B; אלקים] אלים A.

verses.translation: Woe{H188} to them, to the sages{H2450} and to the Perushim{H6567}, who tithe{H6237} the mint and the dill and the pomegranate{H7416}, but rob{H1497} — abandoning — that which is more weighty{H3513}: these are the judgments{H4941} of the Torah{H8451}, and they are kindness{H2617}, truth{H571}, and faithfulness{H530}. These{H428} sayings{H3982} are fitting to do{H6213}, and not to forget{H7911} them.

one_way_hebrew: The tithe-list is a Jewish farmer's, not a translator's: mint (נענע — the mss' reading; rabbinic Hebrew's own herb-name), dill (שבת — m.Ma'aserot 4:5's tithable herb), and the pomegranate (רמון — one of the land's seven species, Deut 8:8, tithable per m.Ma'aserot 1:3). Greek has mint, dill, cummin.
החסד והאמת והאמונה — kindness, truth, faithfulness: the weighty things named in Hosea's triad-language (Hos 4:1, אין אמת ואין חסד; 2:22 באמונה); Greek κρίσιν, ἔλεος, πίστιν translates a Hebrew list.
translation_notes: הנמנע — so the base ms (D), a corruption of הנענע ('the mint'), as ABEF read; the translation follows the mint.

והגוזלים ענבים — literally 'and who rob grapes,' the base ms's corruption; ABEF read ועוזבים ('and abandon'), G וענבים. Howard's English: 'commit robbery (and leave undone) that which is weightier.' The translation keeps the robbery-verb and the abandoning sense.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק צ״ח (Perek 98) begins here.
Howard's note (23:23): 'The Brit. Lib. ms and ms C break off at this point. Ms D becomes our basic text from here to the end' — from this verse to the end of the gospel the printed base is ms D.
The circulating transcription reads החסד האמת; Howard's text reads החסד והאמת, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (23:23): הנמנע] הנענע ABEF; ענבים] ועוזבים ABEF, וענבים G; והאמת] omit G; לעשות] להעשות A.

verses.translation: Offspring{H2233} of blind{H5787} guides{H5090}, who are punctilious in the matter{H1697} of the gnat and swallow{H1104} the camel{H1581}!

one_way_hebrew: מדקדקים — 'punctilious, exacting': the rabbinic term of art for halakhic scrupulosity (medaqdeq be-mitsvot); Greek διϋλίζοντες ('straining out') pictures the act, the Hebrew names the trait — precision about the gnat, appetite for the camel. יתוש is likewise the rabbinic gnat (b.Shabbat 77b), גמל the largest unclean beast (Lev 11:4): the smallest and biggest impurities of the Hebrew taxonomy.
greek_deviations: 'OFFSPRING of blind guides' (זרע מנהיגים העורים) — Greek has simply 'blind guides': the Hebrew makes them a lineage, as vv. 31-32 will press ('sons of the prophets' killers... deeds of your fathers').

verses.translation: Woe{H188} to you, Perushim{H6567} and sages{H2450}, for you wipe the cups{H3563} and the dishes{H7086} on the outside{H2351}, and their inside{H8432} is full{H4390} of carrion{H5038} and uncleanness{H2932}.

one_way_hebrew: נבלה וטומאה — carrion (H5038) and uncleanness (H2932): the technical impurity-categories of Leviticus itself (Lev 11:40; 5:2-3; 7:21). Greek Matthew has 'extortion and excess' (ἁρπαγῆς καὶ ἀκρασίας) — moral terms; the Hebrew indicts them by their own purity-code: the vessel-washers' insides are levitically defiled.
קערה (H7086) — the dish of the Tabernacle service (Num 7:13ff); שתקנחו — the rabbinic wiping-verb (qinneach) of vessel-cleansing halakhah.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (23:25): שתקנחו] שתנקחו A, תקנחו G; והקערות מבחוץ] transposed A.

verses.translation: Hypocrite — cleanse{H5352} first{H8462} what is inside{H8432}, that what is outside{H2351} may be clean{H2889}.

one_way_hebrew: טהור (H2889) — 'clean': again Leviticus' own verdict-word; the sentence runs on the tahor/tamei axis of the purity laws, not on Greek moral vocabulary.
translation_notes: רחוף — an obscure form in the base ms (D); the other mss read החנף ('the hypocrite' — so A, B, EF in Howard's apparatus), which his English prints as '(Hypocrite)' and the translation follows. Greek has 'thou blind Pharisee.'
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (23:26): רחוף נקה] החנף נקה A, החנף מנקה B, EF similarly; מבחוץ] שבחוץ B.

verses.translation: Woe{H188} to you, sages{H2450} and Perushim{H6567}, hypocrites{H2611}, who are like{H1819} whitened{H3835} graves{H6913}, which seem{H1819} beautiful{H3303} on the outside{H2351} to the sons{H1121} of man{H120}, but within{H8432} them they are full{H4390} of the bones{H6106} of the dead{H4191} and of filth.

one_way_hebrew: קברים המלובנים — 'whitened graves': the Hebrew reflects the actual Jewish practice of whitewashing tombs before the festivals so pilgrims would not contract corpse-uncleanness (m.Sheqalim 1:1, 'on the fifteenth of Adar... they mark the graves'); the woe only bites where Num 19:16's corpse-impurity law is in force — a grave defiles precisely the one who cannot see it.
מטונפים — rabbinic Hebrew's word for the filthy (tinnef); another living-register term without biblical Strong's.
translation_notes: יבין — so the base ms (D), a corruption; ABEF read יפים ('beautiful'), which Howard's English follows ('appear... (beautiful)') and the translation adopts (tagged H3303 by the intended word).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (23:27): יבין] יפים ABEF; אדם] האדם EG; ובתוכן] ובתוכם ABF.

verses.translation: So{H3651} you appear{H7200} on the outside{H2351} righteous{H6662} to the sons{H1121} of man{H120}, but within{H7130} you, you are full{H4390} of hypocrisy{H2613} and wickedness{H7564}.

one_way_hebrew: חנפה (H2613) — Jeremiah's noun: 'from the prophets of Jerusalem is profaneness (חנפה) gone forth into all the land' (Jer 23:15) — the only place Scripture uses it, and it is Jerusalem's religious leaders there too.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (23:28): מלאות] מלאים B; ובקרבכם] בקרבכם F; אדם] האדם A.

verses.translation: Woe{H188} to them — hypocrites{H2611} and Perushim{H6567} and sages{H2450} — for you build{H1129} the graves{H6913} of the prophets{H5030} and honor{H3513} the monuments{H6725} of the righteous{H6662},

one_way_hebrew: ציוני (the mss' reading behind the base's צאני) — the ציון (H6725) is Scripture's own word for a prophet's grave-marker: 'What monument (ציון) is that?... It is the grave of the man of God' (2 Kgs 23:17; cf. Ezek 39:15; Jer 31:21). Greek 'adorn the tombs (μνημεῖα)' is generic; the Hebrew names the prophet-marker with the prophet-marker's word.
translation_notes: צאני — so the base ms (D), a corruption of ציוני ('the monuments of'), as ABEF read; ms A reorders the clause (וציוני הצדיקים תכבדו). Howard's English: 'glorify the (monuments) of the righteous.'
textual_notes: The circulating transcription reads קבלי and ורכבדו; Howard's text reads קברי and ותכבדו, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (23:29): להם] לכם ABEFG; ותכבדו צאני הצדיקים] omit G; צאני] ציוני ABEF.

verses.translation: and you say{H559}: If we had been{H1961} in the days{H3117} of our fathers{H1}, we would not have allowed{H3240} [the killing] in the days{H3117} of the prophets{H5030}.

translation_notes: The base ms's sentence is elliptical ('we would not have allowed... in the days of the prophets'); ms A reads להמית ('to put [the prophets] to death') for the second בימי, giving the full sense, and Howard's English prints 'we would not have permitted [them] (to put) the prophets (to death).' The translation supplies the bracketed sense.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (23:30): בימי²] להמית A.

verses.translation: In this{H2063} you testify{H5749} against{H5921} yourselves{H6106} that you are sons{H1121} of those who killed{H2026} the prophets{H5030}.

one_way_hebrew: מעידים (H5749) — 'you testify': the Torah's court-verb (Deut 19:18); the woe convicts them by their own mouths, as at Josh 24:22 ('ye are witnesses against yourselves').

verses.translation: And you{H859} behave{H5090} according to the deeds{H4639} of your fathers{H1}.

one_way_hebrew: כמעשה — 'according to the deeds of': Lev 18:3's formula ('after the doings of the land of Egypt... ye shall not do'); the sons repeat the fathers in the Torah's own phrase for inherited practice.
greek_deviations: Greek Matthew commands, with irony: 'Fill ye up then the measure of your fathers' (πληρώσατε). The Hebrew simply states the fact: 'you behave according to the deeds of your fathers' — indictment, not dare.
textual_notes: The circulating transcription reads נוהבים; Howard's text reads נוהגים, corrected here.

verses.translation: Serpents{H5175}, seed{H2233} of vipers{H6848}! How{H349} will you flee{H5127} from the judgment{H1779} of Gehinnom, if you do not return{H7725} in repentance{H8666}?

one_way_hebrew: צפעוני (H6848) — Isaiah's viper (Isa 11:8; 59:5, 'they hatch viper's eggs'); זרע — 'SEED of vipers' recalls Gen 3:15's serpent's seed, sharper than Greek's γεννήματα ('brood').
תשובו בתשובה — the cognate doubling 'return in returning': teshuvah, Hebrew's own word for repentance, doubled for emphasis as only Hebrew doubles.
greek_deviations: THE DOOR IS LEFT OPEN: Greek Matthew's question is closed — 'how can ye escape the damnation of hell?' The Hebrew adds the condition: 'IF YOU DO NOT RETURN IN REPENTANCE.' The woe-chapter ends, in the Hebrew, with repentance still possible — fully in line with the prophets it has been quoting, whose every doom-oracle is an appeal (Ezek 33:11).
textual_notes: The ms spells Gehinnom גיהנם. The transcriber's footnote notes the sentence should end with a question mark.

verses.translation: At that{H1931} time{H6256} Yeshua{H3442} said{H559} to the companies{H2267} of the Jews{H3064}: Therefore, behold{H2009}, I am sending{H7971} to you prophets{H5030} and sages{H2450} and scribes{H5608}; and some of them you will kill{H2026}, and some of them you will torment{H3510} in your houses of assembly, and you will pursue me{H7291} from city{H5892} to city{H5892}.

one_way_hebrew: הנני שולח לכם — 'Behold, I am sending to you': the sending-formula of the prophets' God (Jer 7:25; 25:4, 'I have sent unto you all my servants the prophets'; Mal 3:23, הנה אנכי שלח לכם). The speaker takes up the sentence-frame of the Sender himself.
נביאים וחכמים וסופרים — prophets, sages, scribes: the three offices of the Jewish schools in their own titles.
greek_deviations: No crucifixion: Greek Matthew has 'some of them ye shall kill and CRUCIFY, and some of them shall ye scourge.' The Hebrew reads 'kill' and 'torment' (תכאיבו, H3510 — the pain-verb of Job 5:18) only; ms A adds ותתלו ('and hang'), assimilating toward the Greek.

ותרדפוני — 'you will pursue ME from city to city': the base text turns the persecution of the sent ones onto the sender himself; ms A reads ותרדפום ('pursue THEM') with the Greek, and Howard's English prints '(them).'
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק צ״ט (Perek 99) begins here.
Howard's apparatus (23:34): הנני] אני EF; וחכמים] חכמים F; וסופרים] סופרים BF; ותרדפוני] ותרדפום A, + ותתלו A.

verses.translation: Upon you{H5921} comes the blood{H1818} of every{H3605} righteous one{H6662} poured out{H8210} upon the earth{H776} — from the blood of Hevel{H1893} the righteous{H6662} to the blood of Zecharyah{H2148} son{H1121} of Berechyah{H1296}, whom you killed{H2026} between{H996} the Sanctuary{H1964} and the altar{H4196}.

one_way_hebrew: דם... הנשפך — 'blood poured out': Gen 9:6's idiom (שפך דם); the ledger runs from Hevel (Gen 4:10, 'thy brother's blood crieth') to Zecharyah slain 'in the court of the house of YHWH' (2 Chr 24:21) — the first and last martyrs of the Hebrew canon's order, Genesis to Chronicles: the span only works in the Hebrew Bible's own arrangement.
greek_deviations: The verse continues v. 34's sentence in the Hebrew ('...pursue me from city to city, so that upon you comes all the righteous blood...'); mss ABEF smooth the join with לתת ('in order to place upon you'), which Howard's English prints as '(in order to place).'
translation_notes: צכריה — the base ms (D) spells Zecharyah with צ (a medieval ז/צ interchange); retained as printed.

בן ברכיה — 'son of Berechyah' names the canonical prophet (Zech 1:1), while the Temple-court martyrdom is that of Zechariah son of Jehoiada (2 Chr 24:20-22); ms B resolves the old crux by OMITTING בן ברכיה — a Hebrew copyist correcting toward Chronicles. Howard's apparatus preserves both states of the text.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (23:35): Beginning] + לתת ABEF; בן ברכיה] omit B; מדם] עד דם EF; ולמזבח] והמזבח A; B transposes ההיכל ולמזבח.

verses.translation: In truth{H571} I say{H559} to you that all{H3605} these{H428} things will come{H935} upon this{H2088} generation{H1755},

translation_notes: באמת — 'in truth': here the text uses the Hebrew adverb where elsewhere it keeps אמן; both are native oath-openers (cf. Jer 26:15, כי באמת).

verses.translation: and upon Yerushalayim{H3389}, that kills{H2026} the prophets{H5030} and removes the sent ones{H7971}. How many{H4100} times{H6471} I wanted{H7521} to gather{H622} your children{H1121} as the hen gathers{H622} her chicks{H667} under{H8478} her wings{H3671} — but you were not willing{H7521}.

one_way_hebrew: תחת כנפיה — 'under her wings': Ruth 2:12's blessing ('under whose wings thou art come to trust') and Ps 91:4 (תחת כנפיו תחסה); the gathering-verb אסף is the prophets' ingathering word. The picture is built of the Tanakh's shelter-idioms.
אפרוחיה (H667) — the chicks of Deut 22:6, the Torah's own nest-law word; השלוחים — 'the SENT ones' (the sheluchim — Hebrew's word behind 'apostles').
greek_deviations: No doubled vocative: Greek Matthew cries 'O Jerusalem, Jerusalem...' as a fresh apostrophe; the Hebrew runs on from v. 36 — 'all these things will come upon this generation AND UPON YERUSHALAYIM that kills the prophets' — one sentence of judgment, then the lament.

ולא רצית — 'you (Jerusalem, singular) were not willing,' answering רציתי ('I wanted'): wanted and not-wanted, the whole tragedy in one Hebrew verb-pair (רצה). Greek ἠθελήσατε is plural and loses the echo.
translation_notes: ומסלקת — 'removes, does away with' (rabbinic סלק); ms A reads ומסקלת ('and STONES'), matching Greek λιθοβολοῦσα ('stoning') — a one-letter metathesis dividing the readings. תרנגולת — the hen, rabbinic Hebrew's own bird-name (no biblical Strong's).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (23:37): ומסלקת] ומסקלת A; התרנגולת] + את G; רצית] רציתם BG.
The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew reads the doubled 'Yerushalayim, Yerushalayim... and stoned the set-apart ones who were sent to you,' with the Greek.

verses.translation: Therefore{H3651} you{H859} will leave{H5800} your houses{H1004} desolate{H2723}.

one_way_hebrew: בתיכם חרבות — 'your houses desolate': Jeremiah's Temple-sentence in Jeremiah's noun — 'this house shall become a desolation (לחרבה)' (Jer 22:5, sworn by YHWH himself; cf. Isa 64:10). Greek ἔρημος translates it.
greek_deviations: 'Your HOUSES' — plural — where Greek has 'your house' (singular, the Temple): the Hebrew widens the desolation from the Sanctuary to their dwellings, Jer 22:5's oracle generalized.

verses.translation: In truth{H571} I say{H559} to you: you will not see me{H7200} from now onward until{H5704} you say{H559}: Blessed{H1288} is our Savior{H3467}.

greek_deviations: ברוך מושיענו — 'Blessed is OUR SAVIOR': where Greek Matthew has Ps 118:26, 'Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord,' the Hebrew gives the cry the crowd actually raised at the entry in this text — 'Hoshana, our Savior' (21:9, הושענא מושיענו). The condition of seeing him again is Jerusalem's own repetition of the entry-confession, and מושיענו carries the name ישו״ע inside it. No Shem Tov ms assimilates the verse to the psalm.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus records no variant for 23:39 — the reading ברוך מושיענו is uniform across the family.

chapter_notes.summary: Matthew 23 in the Shem Tov Hebrew: (1) 23:3 reads the SINGULAR — 'all that HE says to you, keep and do' (Moses, from Moses' seat), 'but according to their ORDINANCES (תקנותיהם, the rabbis' own taqqanot) and deeds do not do' — where Greek Matthew has 'all whatsoever THEY bid you.' The base ms alone keeps the singular; ABDEFG read the plural with the Greek. The Hebrew sentence is coherent Torah-loyalism: Moses' word yes, their enactments no. (2) The oath-woes argue in Mishnaic categories — חייב/אינו חייב ('liable/not liable'), swearing vs vowing, and הנקדש ('what is dedicated,' heqdesh) instead of Greek's 'gold of the temple' (vv. 16-22). Verse 16 is present (the missing verse in this family is 23:21, 'omitted by all mss' per Howard's apparatus; the text runs 20→22, so 'heaven' never enters the oath-chain). (3) The tithe-woe lists mint, dill, and POMEGRANATE (a seven-species tithable fruit; Greek: cummin), and the weighty things are 'kindness, truth, and faithfulness' (v. 23). The cup-woe indicts by purity-law: full of נבלה וטומאה, 'carrion and uncleanness' (v. 25), not Greek's 'extortion and excess.' The tomb-woe presumes the Jewish whitewashing of graves against corpse-impurity (v. 27), and v. 29's grave-'monuments' are ציונים — 2 Kgs 23:17's word for a prophet's marker. (4) 23:33 leaves the door open: 'how will you flee from the judgment of Gehinnom IF YOU DO NOT RETURN IN REPENTANCE (תשובו בתשובה)?' — the teshuvah condition is absent from the Greek. (5) 23:34 has no crucifixion ('kill... torment'; ms A adds 'hang'), and reads 'you will pursue ME from city to city.' 23:35 runs from Hevel to Zecharyah — Genesis to Chronicles, the Hebrew canon's own span; ms B omits 'son of Berechyah,' the copyist's correction of the old crux toward 2 Chr 24 (base ms D spells צכריה). (6) 23:37-39: no doubled 'Jerusalem, Jerusalem' — the judgment sentence runs on from v. 36; 'your HOUSES desolate' (plural; Jer 22:5); and the closing condition is 'until you say: Blessed is OUR SAVIOR (ברוך מושיענו)' — the entry-cry of 21:9, not the Ps 118:26 quotation of the Greek. (7) From 23:23 the Brit. Lib. ms and C break off and ms D is Howard's base to the end of the gospel. Perek marks: vv. 1 (96), 13 (97), 23 (98), 34 (99).
